summary: Unclear routing determinism after AZ failover causing cross-region egress and latency spikes
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent p95 latency spikes and unexpected cross-region egress immediately after an availability-zone (AZ) failover in their us-east region. They believe regional pinning should prevent routing to eu-west but see a subset (~2-3%) of requests egressing to eu-west for ~10-20 minutes after the failover.

Impact: Elevated p95 for token generation (from ~120ms to ~720ms) for a portion of traffic; affects user-facing inference latency for BrightHealth AI clinical triage flow. No request failures observed, primarily latency degradation and higher egress cost.

Environment: Dedicated capacity, strict residency enabled (customer pinned to us-east), model redwood/open-7b-v1, production. AZ failover was triggered by a cloud provider maintenance event noted 2026-03-11 22:30 UTC.

Observed behavior: After the AZ failover, about 2-3% of requests for ~15 minutes were routed to eu-west serving nodes resulting in ~600ms additional network RTT and increased token latencies. DNS lookups from our edge proxies showed mixed A records pointing to us-east and eu-west.

Expected behavior: With strict residency + pin, all inference requests should remain within us-east and never egress to eu-west.

Customer-provided artifacts: sample request IDs and timestamps included in logs section.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer has strict residency toggled to 'us-east' in their tenant config on Dedicated.
2) Simulate an AZ-level capacity degradation or mark an AZ unhealthy in the load balancer (internal staging).
3) Send steady inference traffic pinned to redwood/open-7b-v1 at 100 req/s and monitor per-request egress region and p95 latency.
4) Observe whether a small percentage of requests are routed out-of-region for short windows after failover events.

DNS edge logs: at 22:30:58Z cached A for service-proxy.us-east had TTL=18s; on cache miss resolver returned two A records (us-east, eu-west) due to backend rollout state
Proxy trace: sticky session cookie present for 98% of sessions; tie-breaker weight used for node selection was 'least-loaded' and returned eu-west node for some requests during AZ reconvergence
comments: BrightHealth AI (customer) - 2026-03-12: 'We see short bursts of requests hitting eu-west immediately after the AZ maintenance window. Can you confirm why pinning didn't keep traffic in us-east?'

Support (Aisha) - 2026-03-12: 'Thanks for the report — we're collecting traces and DNS responses. Can you share a couple of example request IDs? Also confirm if you have any per-tenant DNS overrides.'
Customer - 2026-03-12: 'Provided three request IDs via secure attachment. No custom DNS overrides on their side.'

SRE (Marco) - 2026-03-13: 'I've pulled edge resolver logs and observed transient mixed A responses from our control plane during AZ reconvergence. Opening INT-3421 to validate controller's tiebreaker behavior.'

Support - 2026-03-14: 'We've reproduced similar behavior in staging with simulated AZ failover. Hypothesis: DNS pool population and the runtime's node-selection tiebreaker sometimes choose a geographically-different peer during a short window despite strict tenancy pin, when in-AZ capacity is temporarily below per-node thresholds. Working on mitigation.'
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: DNS/Resolver race — control plane briefly advertises nodes from neighboring regions while reconciling healthy us-east nodes, causing some resolvers to receive multi-region A sets.

Hypothesis 2: Node-selection tiebreaker weight prioritizes 'least-loaded' rather than strict residency during reconvergence; if us-east nodes are reporting heavy ephemeral load, tie-breaker picks eu-west node even for pinned requests.
Hypothesis 3: Sticky pin metadata TTL mismatch between edge caches and control plane leads to a window where edge cache returns stale negative for local nodes and triggers fallback to broader pool.
Staging reproduction: Simulated AZ outage in staging produced ~1.8% cross-region egress during 10-20s windows; matches customer magnitude after scaling reconverge delays are introduced.
Captured traces and resolver outputs saved to INT-3421 for deeper debugger session.
resolution:
Mitigation steps provided to customer: (1) Recommended temporary worked-around config: increase residency pin health check thresholds to delay failover selection and set per-tenant node-selection policy to 'prefer-local' in Dedicated console. (2) SRE rolled a control-plane config change to prefer strict-region nodes over 'least-loaded' tie-breaker during reconvergence windows (INT-3421). (3) Shorter-term: edge resolver TTL alignment patch scheduled.

Follow-up actions: (a) ENG to ship control-plane fix to enforce 'region-stickiness' during reconverge (tracking PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rt/commit/af3b2c1) (b) QA to run AZ-failover chaos test against Dedicated fleets (owner: Marco Diaz) (c) CS to confirm with BrightHealth AI after config change.

Status: Workaround applied and control-plane config rolled to canary; monitoring shows cross-region egress reduced to <0.1% in canary ring. Customer informed and asked to validate traffic after next maintenance window.
